newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas-Steady amid a very quiet market.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas-Steady amid a very quiet market.

text.p: Singapore light distillates quotes were steady as market discussions were very thin with hardly any bids and offers seen, traders said on Friday.
They said prices held steady but fundamentals on the gasoline market remained weak while naphtha appeared healthy.
Traders said while regional buying interest for naphtha was thin, levels remained supported by a strong European market and crude gains.
They said the East-West spreads were narrow but attractive freight rates would draw east cargoes west, boosting levels in Singapore.
While persistant talks remained that there are potential naphtha demand from Thailand, no deals were seen done yet.
Traders said Indonesia naphtha exports were also expected to be thin as a crude unit at the Cilacap refinery will close from August 13 for 35 days.
Asia's gasoline market continue to be depressed amid thin buying interests.

Stocks figures from Singapore's trade development board on Thursday showed a build of over 1.8 million barrels of light distillates stocks. Stocks were at 8.016 million barrels, highest since April 1994.
The naphtha swaps rose, helped by a strong European market and gains seen in overnight crudes.
August was last quoted at $22.00/$22.25 and September at $21.85/$22.05, up by 25-30 cents from Thursday's quotes.
